edges.description: Seizures begin in the first year, before the atrophy progresses, so a developmental cause is at least as likely as neuron loss. The edge is kept as a proposed link.

nodes.description: Congenic Gtpbp1 knockout mice on the C57BL/6J background develop ataxia by six weeks and die by eight weeks, with degeneration of cerebellar, dentate gyrus, cortical layer IV and retinal neurons. Gtpbp1 knockouts on a mixed background have no overt phenotype, so the disease depends on the strain's tRNA deficiency.
The atrophy mainly affects the cerebellum.

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense and missense variants reduce GTPBP1 mRNA and protein in patient fibroblasts. GTPBP1 is a cytoplasmic translational GTPase that, like eEF1A, delivers aminoacyl-tRNA to the ribosomal A site, but releases it slowly, which suits it to a surveillance role rather than to bulk elongation. It also stimulates exosomal degradation of mRNA in elongation complexes.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of unconventional mammalian translational GTPases GTPBP1 and GTPBP2.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that GTPBP1 possesses eEF1A-like elongation activity, delivering cognate aminoacyl-transfer RNA (aa-tRNA) to the ribosomal A site in a GTP-dependent manner. It also stimulates exosomal degradation of mRNAs in elongation complexes.

evidence.reference_title: Structural mechanism of mRNA decoding by mammalian GTPase GTPBP1.
evidence.snippet: Similarly to eEF1A, GTPBP1 delivers aminoacyl-tRNA to the ribosome, but the ensuing GTPBP1-mediated elongation is slow.

nodes.description: In Gtpbp1-deficient mice, cerebellar granule cells, dentate gyrus granule cells, cortical layer IV neurons and retinal neurons die from about four weeks of age, the mice become ataxic by six weeks and die by eight weeks. Reduced mTORC1 signaling in the vulnerable neurons accelerates this death. Patients show progressive brain atrophy that mainly affects the cerebellum, with the progressive spasticity and movement disorder of a neurodegenerative course.

Inhibiting mTOR with rapamycin speeds up neuron death, so the fall in mTORC1 signaling worsens degeneration rather than protecting against it.

nodes.description: Without GTPBP1, ribosomes that pause at codons whose tRNA is scarce are not rescued. In Gtpbp1 knockout mice on the C57BL/6J background, which carries a processing mutation in the brain-specific arginine tRNA gene n-Tr20, ribosome occupancy rises at AGA codons in the cerebellum. GTPBP1 and its paralog GTPBP2 are thought to act non-redundantly in the same rescue pathway. Whether the same pausing occurs in human neurons is not known; it was not seen in fibroblasts from GTPBP2-deficient patients.
